Two stadiums in Chaweng share the week: Phetchbuncha Stadium fights on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, and Samui International Muay Thai Stadium on Tuesday, Friday and Sunday, both from about 21:00 until around midnight. There are no fights on Thursday. Tickets cost 1,500 THB (stadium seat), 2,000 THB (ringside) and 2,500 THB (VIP), with a 3,000 THB VIP premium at Samui International. Buy at the box office or book reserved seats with us, never from street touts.

This page is about watching a fight. If you want to train, see Muay Thai training on Koh Samui. Schedules and prices below were checked against the stadiums' own listings and 2026 guides at the start of November 2026.

The first bout often starts a little late. On Buddhist holidays, when alcohol sales are banned in shops, cards can change; the 2027 holy days are 21 February, 20 May, 18–19 July and about 15 October.

Samui International's own website lists half price for children aged 6–10 and free entry under 6. Booked through us, reserved fight tickets cost the same adult prices, with a child rate at Phetchbuncha for children under 140 cm (750 THB standard, 1,000 THB ringside). Counter prices on the night can be higher than advance prices, and popular nights in high season sell out of ringside seats.

Phetchbuncha Stadium

Phetchbuncha (also written Phetch Buncha) is at Chaweng Yai Soi 13, off the Chaweng to Choeng Mon road, an easy walk or short ride from central Chaweng hotels; show the address to your driver. It fights on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday from about 21:00, with a card of about six bouts. It is the more local-feeling of the two, and it is air-conditioned. Advertising cubes on the ring corners can block part of the view from some side seats, so sit square to the ring and arrive about 20 minutes early. Directions to Phetchbuncha Stadium.

Samui International Muay Thai Stadium

Samui International is a few minutes' drive from the main Chaweng resorts and about 400 m from Phetchbuncha. It fights on Tuesday, Friday and Sunday: gates open at 20:00 and the first fight is listed for 21:30, with the night ending around midnight. It has the bigger production, a wider spread of seat levels and a VIP lounge. It is fan-cooled rather than air-conditioned, so wear something light. Directions to Samui International Muay Thai Stadium.

Which seat to buy

  • Standard (1,500 THB): fine for a first visit and for families. The seats are hard, so a cushion helps for a three-hour card.
  • Ringside (2,000 THB): the best value if you care about the fights. You hear the kicks land and see the corners at work, and the view is similar from any ringside seat, so arriving early matters less.
  • VIP (2,500–3,000 THB): sofa seats and a little more space, worth it for a special occasion or a group that wants to sit together.

Book ringside ahead for Friday and Saturday from mid-December to April, when tour groups buy blocks of seats.

What happens on the night

A card runs from about six to eight bouts, usually starting with young local fighters and building to the main event, with foreign fighters from Samui's training camps often on the bill. Each bout opens with the wai kru ram muay, a slow ritual dance in which the fighters honour their teachers, wearing the mongkhon headband. A live band of pipe and drums (sarama) plays throughout and speeds up as the action builds. Professional bouts are five rounds of 3 minutes, sometimes fewer on tourist cards. You will see locals betting with hand signals near the ring; stay out of it.

  • Drinks and snacks are sold inside; a small beer costs about 140 THB.
  • Photos: phone photos and video for personal use are normal; flash in fighters' faces and blocking others' views are not. Professional camera gear may need permission.
  • Dress: casual is fine. Shoulders covered is polite but not enforced.
  • Be ready for blood: this is a full-contact sport and fighters get hurt, including on the early cards with teenage fighters.

Bringing children

Children are allowed at both stadiums, and many families go. Phetchbuncha offers a child rate through us for children under 140 cm; Samui International lists half price for ages 6–10 and free entry under 6 at its own box office. Fights finish around midnight and the music is loud, so bring ear defenders for small children and choose standard seats a few rows back rather than ringside. If combat sports upset your children, a walking street or fire show is a better night out.

Getting there and back

Both stadiums are in Chaweng. From central Chaweng it is a 5–15 minute walk or a short Grab (about 80–120 THB). From Lamai, Bophut or Choeng Mon allow 15–25 minutes by Grab or taxi; agree taxi fares before you get in. After midnight Grab works but can surge, and songthaews have stopped. Don't ride a scooter if you've been drinking. Transfers are not included with our tickets; we can arrange a private return van on request. More: getting around Koh Samui.

Buying tickets: box office, us or touts?

  • The stadium box office, on the night or earlier the same day.
  • The stadiums' own websites and licensed agents, including our reserved seats with confirmation by email or WhatsApp.
  • Street touts and flyer sellers on Chaweng Beach Road, who sometimes sell the wrong night, the wrong stadium or the cheapest seats at a mark-up.

Closed and occasional venues

Chaweng Stadium, the island's older third stadium, has been reported closed in 2026, and we found no current fight schedule in Lamai, although an undated listing mentions Saturday bouts at a ring in central Lamai. Occasional charity and special fight nights are held around the island; they appear on Koh Samui events when announced.

Make a night of it

The stadiums sit between the Chaweng Lake area and the beach, so a fight fits neatly into a night out. On Friday and Saturday, eat at Chaweng Walking Street by the lake from about 18:00 (see walking streets), watch the card from 21:00, then walk to the beach for the ARKbar fire show or Soi Green Mango after midnight. Full plan: Chaweng nightlife and our Chaweng guide.

Train yourself

Watching a fight is the best introduction to training. Samui's camps run drop-in classes from about 500 THB in 2026, with beginner groups every morning and afternoon. See Muay Thai training on Koh Samui. Between fight nights, the sea is the other half of a Samui week: the Pig Island speedboat tour runs every day of the year, and the Ang Thong speedboat tour resumes on 16 December after the park's annual closure.
